text:
mika: Heads up — I'm seeing a spike in 5xxs on the streaming endpoints during the canary for streaming-throttler-v2. Clients are reconnecting and some streams are resuming but responses are duplicated for a subset of users.

raj: Which route/pool? any logs or request ids? :eyes:

mika: Sample log excerpt:
```
2026-03-18T15:12:03Z INFO stream_start client_id=cli-987 route=/v1/stream model=redwood-v2 pool=pool-a stream_id=st-42
2026-03-18T15:12:04Z WARN stream_pause client_id=cli-987 reason=backpressure sent=token=abc123
2026-03-18T15:12:05Z INFO stream_resume_attempt client_id=cli-987 resume_token=abc123 -> routed_to=pool-b
2026-03-18T15:12:05Z ERROR resume_rejected client_id=cli-987 reason=pool-mismatch expected_pool=pool-a actual=pool-b
2026-03-18T15:12:05Z INFO stream_recreate client_id=cli-987 new_stream_id=st-43 duplicate_output=true
```

sophie: Is this coming from the throttler change from last night? I remember PR #432 added early 429s with Retry-After to force backpressure.

mika: Exactly. The client treats the 429 as a disconnect and attempts a resume with the same token. But the resume token doesn't include the serving pool id or model variant, and smart routing can send the resume to a different pool (pool-b) that doesn't have the KV cache — so the model re-generates the tail of the stream => duplicate chunks returned.

raj: Two problems: 1) resume token entropy is too small (no pool/model context). 2) telemetry doesn't correlate start/resume/recreate so console shows "healthy" overall while per-route duplicate rate spikes. We need both a token fix and better traces.

mika: Also hitting quota weirdness: quota-agent currently charges tokens again on resume because we treat resumed tokens as new requests. That inflates billing and sometimes crosses customer quota boundaries causing further throttles (a feedback loop).

sophie: UX note — the rollout page in Console currently rolls up these metrics and hides streaming-specific events. We should surface metrics like "stream resumes / min", "resume rejects", and "duplicate-chunk rate" on the rollout panel so PMs can see impact immediately.

raj: Proposed immediate actions:
- include pool-id, model-version, region in resume token (signed)
- validate token server-side and reject with explicit 409 + reason if pool mismatch
- add correlation_id to all stream lifecycle events (start/pause/resume/recreate)
- add streaming-specific panels/alerts in Console (resume_reject_rate > 0.5% => P2)

mika: For quick mitigation, we can flip the new throttler off in canary and push a client patch so that clients treat 429+Retry-After as a pause (do not attempt resume for 10s). That prevents immediate resume loops.

ops-sre: What will the server response look like for rejected resume? example?

mika: Example headers and response we saw:
```
> GET /v1/stream?stream_id=st-42 HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.example
> X-Resume-Token: abc123
> X-Client-Stream-ID: st-42

< HTTP/1.1 409 Resume-Token-Rejected
< Content-Type: application/json
< X-Resume-Reason: pool-mismatch
{"error":"resume_token_rejected","reason":"pool-mismatch","expected_pool":"pool-a","node":"pool-b-12"}
```

raj: I'll open a patch PR to extend the token, add server-side validation, and annotate traces. Sophie — can you own Console panels/alert? I'd like to wire the resume_reject metric into the rollout healthscore.

sophie: On it. I'll add two panels and one alert: resume_rate, resume_reject_rate, duplicate_chunk_rate. Also will add a tooltip explaining "why resume rejects happen" for non-engineer PMs.

deploy-bot: deploy: canary rollback streaming-throttler-v2 -> SUCCESS (1796004355) :white_check_mark:

mika: Thanks — reverting should stop the immediate customer impact. I'll keep monitoring for duplicate outputs and quota spikes.

sophie: Thanks team. Followups: PRs for token + traces + console panels. Can we prioritize the token fix for this week?

raj: Yes, I'll target a patch today and request an expedited review.

ops-sre: Noted — I'll set a temporary alert on "duplicate_chunk_rate" and mute noisy alarms for the canary window.

mika: Monitoring now: duplicate_chunk_rate trending down after rollback. Closing for now but keeping follow-up tickets. :thumbsup:
